source.title: The Parietal Eye of Lizards (Pogona vitticeps) Needs Light at a Wavelength Lower than 580 nm to Activate Light-Dependent Magnetoreception

quote: Lizards with light-absorption filters that cut out light with wavelengths lower than 380 nm were found to respond to the EMF.
note: Name: Pogona vitticeps (Ahl, 1926), Agamidae, VALID on the Reptile Database page reptile-database.reptarium.cz/Pogona/vitticeps (opened); repo gbif-names.tsv has no row. DOI checked on Crossref (title, sole author, Animals 10, issue 3, issued 2020-03-15, CC BY 4.0 licence URL; article page metadata lists CC BY 3.0, footer CC BY 4.0 per the fetch). The stimulus is an extremely low frequency electromagnetic field with magnetic and electric components that were not separated, so this is not a test of the geomagnetic field, and the response is a tail-lift count, a behavioural proxy. Experiments 1 and 2, with a filter cutting light below 580 nm, showed no significant EMF-control difference (combined p = 0.67 for the increase and p = 0.41 for the ratio; Experiment 3 EMF vs control p = 0.02 for both measures, per the fetch summary and the Abstract; the sentence reporting the null is too long to quote). The title's claim of light-dependent magnetoreception is the author's interpretation. Small sample (8 per crossover group) and juveniles in Experiment 1 differ from adults in Experiment 2.
